sarf-135.text: <bdi>مَبْنِيّ</bdi>: {{c1::every <bdi>حَرْف</bdi>, and the <bdi>مَاضِي</bdi> and the <bdi>أَمْر</bdi>}}, and {{c2::some}} <bdi>أَسْمَاء</bdi>. <bdi>مُعْرَب</bdi>: the <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi>, and {{c2::most}} <bdi>أَسْمَاء</bdi>
sarf-135.extra: a <bdi>مَبْنِيّ اِسْم</bdi> resembles a <bdi>حَرْف</bdi> — Tasheel ch. 2 (nahw-224, nahw-225)

new.front: What causes <bdi>إِعْرَاب</bdi>, the change at the end of a <bdi>مُعْرَب</bdi> word?
new.back: External factors: the words that govern it, its <bdi>عَوَامِل</bdi>. The term is the maṣdar of <bdi>أَعْرَبَ يُعْرِبُ</bdi>.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.front: What are the four <bdi>أَنْوَاع البِنَاء</bdi>, the endings a <bdi>مَبْنِيّ</bdi> word can be fixed on?
new.back: <bdi>سُكُون</bdi>, <bdi>فَتْحَة</bdi>, <bdi>كَسْرَة</bdi> and <bdi>ضَمَّة</bdi> — <bdi>كَمْ</bdi> is <bdi>مَبْنِيّ</bdi> on sukūn, <bdi>أَيْنَ</bdi> on fatḥah, <bdi>هَؤُلَاءِ</bdi> on kasrah, <bdi>حَيْثُ</bdi> on ḍammah
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.back: <bdi>رَفْع</bdi>, <bdi>نَصْب</bdi>, <bdi>جَرّ</bdi> and <bdi>جَزْم</bdi> — a word in each is <bdi>مَرْفُوع</bdi>, <bdi>مَنْصُوب</bdi>, <bdi>مَجْرُور</bdi> or <bdi>مَجْزُوم</bdi>
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.front: What are the two kinds of <bdi>عَلَامَة الإِعْرَاب</bdi>?
new.back: <bdi>بِالحَرَكَات</bdi>, by vowel signs: ḍammah, fatḥah, kasrah, sukūn. <bdi>بِالحُرُوف</bdi>, by letters such as <bdi>و</bdi> or <bdi>ا</bdi>, where only the changing letter is the sign: <bdi>مُسْلِمُونَ</bdi>, <bdi>مُسْلِمِينَ</bdi>.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.front: What is the sign of each of the four <bdi>إِعْرَاب</bdi> states?
new.back: <bdi>رَفْع</bdi>: a ḍammah · <bdi>نَصْب</bdi>: a fatḥah · <bdi>جَرّ</bdi>: a kasrah · <bdi>جَزْم</bdi>: a sukūn — each can be replaced by a substitute, such as a letter
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.front: Which <bdi>إِعْرَاب</bdi> state belongs only to the <bdi>اِسْم</bdi>, and which only to the <bdi>فِعْل</bdi>?
new.back: <bdi>جَرّ</bdi> only to the <bdi>اِسْم</bdi>, and <bdi>جَزْم</bdi> only to the <bdi>فِعْل</bdi>. Both share <bdi>رَفْع</bdi> and <bdi>نَصْب</bdi>.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.meaning: the iʿrāb a <bdi>مُعْرَب</bdi> word carries on its own ending — as opposed to the iʿrāb of a position
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.meaning: iʿrāb of position — a <bdi>مَبْنِيّ</bdi> word fills a slot that has a state, but can't show it
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.front: Why does a <bdi>مَبْنِيّ اِسْم</bdi> still have <bdi>إِعْرَاب مَحَلِّيّ</bdi>?
new.back: Every <bdi>اِسْم</bdi> in a sentence fills a position that has a grammatical state. The <bdi>مَبْنِيّ</bdi> word can't show it, so its state is one of position: in <bdi>جَاءَ هَذَا</bdi>, <bdi>هَذَا</bdi> is <bdi>مَبْنِيّ</bdi> but stands in the place of <bdi>رَفْع</bdi>, as the <bdi>فَاعِل</bdi>.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.meaning: visible iʿrāb — the ending of a <bdi>مُعْرَب</bdi> word shows its state
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.meaning: hidden iʿrāb — a <bdi>مُعْرَب</bdi> word whose ending can't show its state
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.back: The <bdi>اِسْم مَقْصُور</bdi>, ending in an alif (<bdi>الفَتَى</bdi>); the <bdi>اِسْم مَنْقُوص</bdi>, ending in a <bdi>ي</bdi> after a kasrah (<bdi>القَاضِي</bdi>); an <bdi>اِسْم</bdi> joined to the speaker's <bdi>ي</bdi> (<bdi>كِتَابِي</bdi>); and a <bdi>مُضَارِع</bdi> ending in a weak letter (<bdi>يَسْعَى</bdi>, <bdi>يَدْعُو</bdi>, <bdi>يَرْمِي</bdi>).
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.front: Why does <bdi>الفَتَى</bdi> never show its state, while <bdi>القَاضِي</bdi> shows one of the three?
new.back: <bdi>الفَتَى</bdi> ends in an alif, which can't carry any vowel, so all three states are <bdi>مُقَدَّر</bdi>. The <bdi>ي</bdi> of <bdi>القَاضِي</bdi> carries a fatḥah (<bdi>رَأَيْتُ القَاضِيَ</bdi>), but a ḍammah or kasrah on it is too heavy, so <bdi>رَفْع</bdi> and <bdi>جَرّ</bdi> are <bdi>مُقَدَّر</bdi>.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.front: What does a parser mean by <bdi>لَا مَحَلَّ لَهُ مِنَ الإِعْرَاب</bdi>, said of a <bdi>حَرْف</bdi>?
new.back: That it has no place in iʿrāb at all: a <bdi>حَرْف</bdi> is always <bdi>مَبْنِيّ</bdi>, and never fills a position that has a grammatical state.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.front: Which two endings make a <bdi>مُضَارِع مَبْنِيّ</bdi>, and on what is it built?
new.back: <bdi>نُون النِّسْوَة</bdi>, on sukūn (<bdi>يَكْتُبْنَ</bdi>); and <bdi>نُون التَّوْكِيد</bdi> joined directly, on fatḥah (<bdi>لَيَكْتُبَنَّ</bdi>)
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.front: Why is the relative pronoun <bdi>الَّذِي مَبْنِيّ</bdi>?
new.back: It resembles a <bdi>حَرْف</bdi> in dependence: it needs other words, its <bdi>صِلَة</bdi>, to complete its meaning. This is <bdi>الشَّبَه الافْتِقَارِيّ</bdi>.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13

new.front: Why are pronouns such as <bdi>تُ</bdi> and <bdi>نَا مَبْنِيّ</bdi>?
new.back: They resemble a <bdi>حَرْف</bdi> in form: each is built of fewer than three letters. This is <bdi>الشَّبَه الوَضْعِيّ</bdi>.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-13
